names.note: Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 27. октобар ст. ст., „Св. Андреј кнез Смоленски.“ — «Св.» is "saint" and not a rank and «кнез» is the `prince` grade this corpus keeps in `types`, so both come off and the bare name keeps the by-name the heading prints. The by-name is kept because four folders in this corpus already hold the bare «Андреј» — `andrew-companion-of-paul`, `andrew-of-crete`, `andrew-the-monk-martyr-of-crete` and `andrew-the-presbyter-confessor` — so a bare forename would fold on a forename, and section 6 asks for the fullest form the calendar gives. `sr-foldnew.mjs` reports 0 other holders for both keys the folder would add.

death.note: The Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the Julian 27 October: „Упокојио се у Господу мирно 1390. год.“ — he reposed in the Lord peacefully in 1390. The entry gives no birth year, no age and no century beside it, so there is no `birth`. The other year it prints, 1540, is the finding of his relics and not a date of his life.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.11.2025 (27. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. Андреј кнез Смоленски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry and the only new folder on it. «кнез» is the `prince` this folder takes and the heading gives no second rank word: it does not say Преподобни, Праведни or Чудотворац, so there is no `venerable`, no `righteous` and no `wonderworker` here — the body says his RELICS are wonderworking, which is a fact about the relics and not a title the calendar gives the man. The entry is three sentences and the life says so. NO `locations`: the only place in the whole entry is «један манастир», one monastery, unnamed, and Smolensk reaches the page only inside the by-name. NO `office`: «црквењак», a sexton or church servant, is not in the four locale packs. NO `related`: the entry names nobody. NO HYMN: the Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about Nestor. THE NEAREST FOLDER AND WHY IT IS NOT HIM: `andrew-prince-of-suzdal`, also a prince, died 1365 and is kept on the Greek 2 June — twenty-five years and a different day apart, and nothing read links them.
